info.name: 48Date Backend API
info.description:
The 48Date backend API. Top level splits by **who calls it** (User = the Flutter app, Admin = the Next.js panel); inside each, one folder per module. Kept in sync with every endpoint change — see postman/README.md.

Request bodies hold clean, always-valid JSON (no inline comments — a comment inside a JSON value is invalid data, not documentation); every field is instead documented in the request’s own Description, right below the body. Fields reused across requests in the same flow (phone numbers, OTP codes, tokens, ids) are collection variables, auto-captured by a response script where the value comes from the API, or editable once up top where it’s user input.

request.description:
Watches core services (PostgreSQL database and Redis) for uptime monitors.

**Who can call:** Public (no authentication required).

**Success:** 200 OK when all monitored dependencies are operational.

**Error:** 503 Service Unavailable if any monitored service is down.

response.name: 200 OK — Healthy
503 Service Unavailable — Dependency Down

item.name: 01 - Auth
item.description: Module 1 — Phone OTP / Google sign-in, account linking, and session management.

request.description:
Starts phone sign-in: checks Redis rate limits, generates a 6-digit code, stores its hash in Redis (5 min TTL) and enqueues the `sms` job (Twilio delivers it; never sent inline). Public — no auth required. Continue with **02 Verify Phone OTP**.

Rate limits: 60 s cooldown between sends to the same phone, 5/hour and 10/day per phone, 20/hour per IP.

The `{{phone}}` variable is shared with **02 Verify Phone OTP** — change it once here (or in the environment) and both requests stay in sync. `{{devOtp}}` is captured automatically from the response below (only present when DEV_MODE is on and Twilio isn’t configured) for **02 Verify Phone OTP** to use.

**Body fields:**

- `phone` (string, required) — E.164 format — must include the country code, e.g. +8801811000001

response.name: 200 OK — Code sent (DEV_MODE, no Twilio credentials)

request.description:
Verifies the code from **01 Request Phone OTP**, finds or creates the user, issues a session (revoking every other session on this account — single active device policy), and returns the token pair. A `BANNED` account is rejected; a `DELETED` account within its 90-day window is restored automatically (`restored: true`). Public — no auth required.

Uses `{{phone}}` and `{{devOtp}}` captured by **01 Request Phone OTP** — run that first. On success, `{{accessToken}}`/`{{refreshToken}}` are captured here for every bearer-auth request below.

**Body fields:**

- `phone` (string, required) — E.164 format, must match the phone used in 01 Request Phone OTP
- `otp` (string, required) — 6-digit code — auto-filled from 01 Request Phone OTP in DEV_MODE; replace with the real SMS code otherwise
- `device` (object, optional) — recorded on the user session:
 - `device.platform` (string, optional) — client platform (case-sensitive, one of: `"android"`, `"ios"`, `"web"`)
 - `device.appVersion` (string, optional) — semver app version string (e.g. `"1.4.0"`)
 - `device.deviceName` (string, optional) — human-readable device model (e.g. `"Pixel 8"`, `"iPhone 15 Pro"`)

request.description:
Verifies the Google ID token (signature, issuer, audience against `GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS`), finds or creates the user by `googleSub`, issues a session (one device at a time). Public — no auth required.

**Body fields:**

- `idToken` (string, required) — from the Google Sign-In SDK on the client; cannot be auto-filled
- `device` (object, optional) — recorded on the user session:
 - `device.platform` (string, optional) — client platform (case-sensitive, one of: `"android"`, `"ios"`, `"web"`)
 - `device.appVersion` (string, optional) — semver app version string (e.g. `"1.4.0"`)
 - `device.deviceName` (string, optional) — human-readable device model (e.g. `"Pixel 8"`, `"iPhone 15 Pro"`)

request.description:
Rotates the refresh token: the presented token is invalidated and a new access/refresh pair is issued for the same session (the session id does not change). Presenting a token that was already rotated or revoked is treated as token theft — the whole session family is revoked and the account must sign in again. Public endpoint (the refresh token itself is the credential) — no bearer header needed.

Uses and replaces `{{refreshToken}}`.

**Body fields:**

- `refreshToken` (string, required) — from 02 Verify Phone OTP, 03 Google Sign-In, or a previous call to this endpoint

request.description:
Same OTP engine as sign-in, purpose `LINK`, with standard rate limits. Checked up front that the phone is not already linked to another account. **Auth:** bearer access token required.

`{{linkPhone}}` is a separate variable from `{{phone}}` (the sign-in number) so you can link a second number without overwriting it. `{{linkDevOtp}}` is captured automatically for **10 Link Phone — Verify OTP**.

**Body fields:**

- `phone` (string, required) — E.164 format, the number to link — different from the sign-in phone

request.description:
Records a user swipe (`PASS` or `LIKE`) synchronously.

**Who can call:** Authenticated user.
**Rules:**
- `targetNickname` is resolved to internal user ID.
- Cannot swipe on oneself (`400 SWIPE_SELF`).
- Cannot swipe on unavailable or blocked user (`409 USER_UNAVAILABLE`).
- Repeating the same action is idempotent.
- `PASS` -> `LIKE` is allowed (recycled profile after 30 days).
- `LIKE` -> `PASS` is forbidden (`409 SWIPE_ALREADY_DECIDED`). A like is permanent.
- When a `LIKE` is mutual, creates a match in Module 4 inside the same transaction and returns popup details.

**Body fields:**
- `targetNickname`: string (required) — Permanent nickname of candidate.
- `action`: string (required, case-sensitive) — `PASS` | `LIKE`.
- `source`: string (optional, case-sensitive) — `DECK` | `PROFILE`. Default `DECK`.
- `runId`: string (optional) — Discovery run UUID if swiped from deck.

**Side effects:** Emits `discovery.swiped` and `discovery.liked` counters; on mutual match, queues `MATCH_NEW` push notification.

**Super Like (DF-05, D-204):**
- Passing `action: 'SUPER_LIKE'` consumes from the user's weekly allowance.
- Sends immediate push notification `SUPER_LIKE_RECEIVED` to recipient.
- Places the sender at the front of the recipient's card deck stack with `isSuperLike: true`.
- If recipient already swiped LIKE or SUPER_LIKE, creates an instant Match popup.

200 Mutual Match Created (Match Popup)

Activates a profile boost for the user (DF-06, D-204, D-205).

**Entitlement:** Consumes from `BOOST_PER_WEEK`.

- Fails with 409 `BOOST_ALREADY_ACTIVE` if a boost is already currently active.
- Fails with 429 `BOOST_EXHAUSTED` if weekly quota is depleted.

request.description:
Undoes the single most recent swipe (DF-07, D-204, D-205).

**Mechanics:**
- Reads `discovery:last_swipe:{userId}` from Redis.
- Fails with 404 `NO_SWIPE_TO_UNDO` if no recent swipe exists.
- Fails with 410 `UNDO_TIME_EXPIRED` if the time window (`rewindTimeLimitMinutes`, default 15 mins) has elapsed.
- Fails with 409 `CANNOT_UNDO_MATCHED_SWIPE` if the swipe already formed an active match (D-204 safe boundary).
- In MVP: All users can undo (paywalls hidden per D-189/D-190/D-197; `rewindAllowedForFree: true`).
- Post-MVP: Rejects with 403 `REWIND_PREMIUM_ONLY` if admin sets `rewindAllowedForFree: false` and user lacks `UNDO_SWIPE` entitlement.
- Deletes the `Swipe` record from PostgreSQL.
- Re-inserts the candidate card onto the front of the user's active Redis deck (`discovery:deck:{runId}`).
- Clears `discovery:last_swipe:{userId}` (1-step undo only, D-204).
- Returns the restored candidate card representation.

**Route Aliases:**
- Primary: `POST /api/v1/discovery/deck/undo`
- Alias: `POST /api/v1/discovery/swipes/undo` (both routes invoke the single-step swipe rewind).

request.description:
Connects to the real-time Socket.IO chat gateway.

### 1. Connection & Handshake
- **Protocol:** Socket.IO v4
- **HTTP Handshake URL:** `{{socketUrl}}/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling&token={{accessToken}}`
- **WebSocket URL (Flutter App):** `ws://localhost:3000/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket&token={{accessToken}}`
- **Authentication:** Pass the Bearer access token either via handshake header:
 `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`
 or query parameter:
 `?token={{accessToken}}`

### 2. Client → Server Events
| Event | Payload | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `joinConversation` | `{"conversationId": "uuid"}` | Join conversation room (`conversation:{id}`). |
| `leaveConversation` | `{"conversationId": "uuid"}` | Leave conversation room. |
| `typing` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "isTyping": true}` | Relay typing indicator to room (relayed only, never stored in DB). |
| `message:delivered` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "upToSeq": 42}` | Advance `deliveredUpToSeq` pointer in `conversation_members`. |
| `message:seen` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "upToSeq": 42}` | Advance `seenUpToSeq` pointer in `conversation_members`. |
| `heartbeat` | `{}` | Refreshes Redis online presence TTL (60s). |

### 3. Server → Client Events
| Event | Payload | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `message:new` | `MessageItemDto` | Full new message (delivered to room and recipient's user room). |
| `conversation:receipt` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "nickname": "str", "deliveredUpToSeq": int, "seenUpToSeq": int}` | Partner's delivery or seen pointer moved. |
| `typing` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "nickname": "str", "isTyping": bool}` | Partner typing status update. |
| `presence` | `{"nickname": "str", "online": bool, "lastSeenAt": "iso"}` | Partner presence status. |
| `conversation:closed` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "reason": "EXPIRED \| BLOCKED"}` | Conversation closed upon match expiry or block.

**Query parameters:**
- `EIO` (string, required): Engine.IO protocol version (`4`).
- `transport` (string, required): Transport mechanism (`polling` for HTTP handshake, `websocket` for Flutter socket).
- `token` (string, optional): Bearer access token for handshake authentication.
| `message:edited` | `{"messageId": "uuid", "conversationId": "uuid", "text": "str", "isEdited": true, "editedAt": "iso"}` | Broadcast when a message is edited. |
| `message:deleted` | `{"messageId": "uuid", "conversationId": "uuid", "isDeleted": true, "deletedAt": "iso"}` | Broadcast when a message is soft-deleted. |

- `cursor` (string, optional): Sequence number threshold for older messages (`seq < cursor`).
- `after` (string, optional): Sequence number threshold for catch-up messages (`seq > after`).
- `limit` (integer, optional): Maximum messages per page (default: 20, max: 50).

request.description:
Sends a message to the conversation synchronously with idempotent retry protection.

Monotonically assigns sequence number `seq`, advances sender's own delivery/seen pointer, touches match `lastActivityAt`, and broadcasts over Socket.IO.

### Supported Sending Methods:
1. **JSON Payload (Pre-uploaded File IDs):** Upload media via `POST /api/v1/files` (`CHAT_IMAGE` or `CHAT_VOICE`), then pass `fileId` (single image/voice) or `fileIds` (multiple images, up to 10).
2. **Direct Multipart Upload (form-data):** In Postman, switch Body mode from `raw` to `form-data` and attach files directly:
 - Single Image or Voice: Key `file` (type: File)
 - Multiple Images: Key `files` (type: File, attach multiple)
 - Add form fields: `type` (`IMAGE` or `VOICE`), `durationSeconds` (for voice, e.g. `14`), `text` (optional caption).

**Path parameters:**
- `conversationId` (string, required): UUID of conversation.

**Body fields:**
- `clientMessageId` (string, optional): Client-generated UUID v4 for safe idempotent retries (auto-generated if omitted).
- `type` (string, required): Message type, case-sensitive allowed values: `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `VOICE`, `SYSTEM`, `DATE`, `GAME`, `DATE_INVITE`.
- `text` (string, optional): Required for TEXT messages, or caption for IMAGE/VOICE, trimmed, max 2000 characters.
- `fileId` (string, optional): UUID v4 of file from `POST /api/v1/files` for single IMAGE or VOICE message.
- `fileIds` (array of string, optional): Array of UUID v4 file IDs for sending multiple photos at once (max 10 photos).
- `durationSeconds` (integer, optional): Duration in seconds for VOICE messages (1 to 120 seconds).

**Weekly Chat Unlocks:**
- Free tier users are limited to 1 chat unlock per week (`CHAT_UNLOCKS_PER_WEEK`).
- The first message sent in a conversation consumes 1 weekly chat unlock.
- Once unlocked, subsequent messages within that conversation are free for both participants.
- If a free user exceeds their weekly unlock quota, the request returns `429 Too Many Requests` with code `LIMIT_REACHED`.

request.description:
Starts a new game or retrieves the active/completed game for this conversation (strictly one game per conversation).

When a new game starts, the AI analyzes both participants' profiles (shared & distinct interests, hobbies, occupation, lifestyle) and generates 10 tailored, personalized 'This or That' dilemma questions (DF-11, D-208) with `isAiGenerated: true` and `category` tags. If AI generation is disabled or fails, the engine seamlessly falls back to 10 active admin-managed questions with `isAiGenerated: false`.

An immutable snapshot of the 10 questions is stored on the game record and an invitation bubble is posted into the chat conversation.

**Path parameters:**
- `conversationId` (UUID, required): Conversation ID owning the game.

**Body fields:**
- `gameType` (string, optional, default: `"THIS_OR_THAT"`): Allowed value: `THIS_OR_THAT` (case-sensitive).
- `conversationId` (string, optional): Also supported directly on `POST /games` payload.

**Notifications sent:** When a new game is created, the partner receives `GAME_INVITE` (push + in-app inbox, target screen `GAME`, `targetParams: { gameId, conversationId }`). Returning an existing game sends nothing.

**Route Aliases:**
- Primary: `POST /api/v1/conversations/:id/games` (with `:id` in the path)
- Alias: `POST /api/v1/games` with JSON body `{ "conversationId": "{{conversationId}}" }`.

request.description:
Retrieves game questions, personal answers, and revealed partner answers.

**No Peeking Rule:**
The server strictly hides the partner's choice for question $N$ until the requesting user has answered question $N$ themselves (`partnerChoice: null`, `partnerAnswered: true/false`). Once answered, both choices and match status (`isMatch`) are immediately revealed.

**Path parameters:**
- `gameId` (UUID, required): Game ID.

response.name: 200 OK — Game State with No-Peeking Masking

request.description:
Submits an answer (`A` or `B`) for a question in an in-progress game.

**Sequential Progression Rule:**
Questions must be answered strictly in order (Question 1 of 10 through Question 10 of 10). Skipping questions or attempting later questions out of sequence returns `400 Bad Request` (`GAME_QUESTION_OUT_OF_ORDER`).

If the partner has already answered this question, the match result is revealed immediately (`isMatch: true/false`). When both players complete all 10 questions, the game status transitions to `COMPLETED`, a result bubble is posted in the chat, and `game:completed` is broadcast over Socket.IO.

**Path parameters:**
- `gameId` (UUID, required): Game ID.

**Body fields:**
- `questionId` (UUID, required): The question ID in the game snapshot.
- `choice` (enum, required): Selected option: `A` or `B` (case-sensitive).

**Notifications sent:** When the last answer completes the game, both players receive `GAME_COMPLETED` (push + in-app inbox, target screen `GAME`).

request.description:
Confirms attendance for a date once its scheduled calendar time has passed (Mobile screens `M / ATTENDANCE` and `M / ATTENDANCE-WAIT`).

### Two-Sided Attendance Confirmation (D-203)
When a date passes its scheduled time, it transitions from `SET` to `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`:
1. **Screen 1 (`ATTENDANCE` — "Did you meet {partner}?"):**
   - User chooses: "Yes, we met" (`attended = true`) or "No, we didn't meet" (`attended = false`).
2. **Screen 2 (`ATTENDANCE-WAIT` — "Your confirmation is saved"):**
   - Displays "We're waiting for {partner}'s response." with status badge "• Awaiting both responses".
   - Provides action buttons "Leave feedback" (proceeds to date ratings) and "Back to matches".

### State Transitions
- **If partner has not confirmed yet:** The date stays in status `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`. The response returns `bothConfirmed: false` and `completed: false`. Partner receives a notification asking them to confirm.
- **If both participants confirm `attended = true`:** The date immediately transitions to `COMPLETED` (`completedAt` is recorded). Socket event `date:completed` is broadcast, the chat date bubble updates to `COMPLETED`, and both participants are notified to leave feedback / rate each other.
- **If either participant confirms `attended = false`:** The date transitions to `NO_SHOW` (and appropriate trust score event is logged).

**Who can call:** Authenticated participant (`proposer` or `receiver`) of the date plan.
**Side effects:** Saves participant's attendance confirmation; transitions date to `COMPLETED` or `NO_SHOW` when both have responded; emits WebSocket events `date:confirmed` or `date:completed`.

**Body fields:**
- `attended` (boolean, required) — `true` ("Yes, we met") or `false` ("No, we didn't meet").
- `note` (string, optional, max 500 characters) — optional attendance comment.

request.description:
Requests 3 AI-generated reply suggestions upon tapping ✨ in the chat.

### Core Rules:
- **Instant Reuse:** If no new message arrived in this conversation since the last request, returns the cached suggestions instantly (`isCached: true`) without consuming a daily tap.
- **Date Nudge:** While the 48-hour clock is running, at least one suggestion casually nudges toward planning a date.
- **Tone Selection:** Gated by the `AI_TONE_SELECT` plan entitlement.

**Path parameters:**
- `conversationId` (UUID, required): The target conversation identifier.

**Body fields:**
- `tone` (string, optional): Desired suggestion tone. Allowed values (case-sensitive): `FLIRTY`, `CASUAL`, `WITTY`.

**Response capture:**
Saves `data.requestId` into collection variable `{{aiRequestId}}`.

request.description:
Retrieves the authenticated user's cursor-paginated notification inbox, newest first, including unread badge count.

**Who can call:** Authenticated user (Bearer token).

**Query params:**
- `cursor` (string, optional): Keyset cursor from previous page.
- `limit` (number, optional): Items per page, default 20 (max 50).

**Every notification has the same shape** (inbox list, `notification:new` socket event and push payload): `id`, `type`, `category`, `title`, `body`, `imageUrl`, `actor` (the other user, or null), `target: { screen, params }`, `createdAt`, `readAt`. Open `target.screen` with the ids in `target.params`.

**Notification types** (case-sensitive `type` values):

| `type` | Sent when / to whom | `target.screen` | `target.params` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MATCH_NEW` | Mutual like or auto-match, to both users | `CHAT` | `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `MATCH_EXPIRING_SOON` | ~6 h before the 48 h clock runs out, to both users | `CHAT` | `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `MATCH_EXPIRED` | The 48 h clock ran out, to both users (inbox only, no push) | `MATCHES` | `matchId` |
| `MESSAGE_NEW` | **Push only, never in the inbox.** Text, photo or voice message to an offline user. Date and game bubbles never send it; they have their own types | `CHAT` | `conversationId` |
| `GAME_INVITE` | A game is started, to the other player | `GAME` | `gameId`, `conversationId` |
| `GAME_COMPLETED` | Both players finished, to both | `GAME` | `gameId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_INVITE_RECEIVED` | Date invite sent, to the invited user | `DATE_DETAIL` | `dateId`, `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_ACCEPTED` | Invite accepted, to the proposer | `DATE_DETAIL` | `dateId`, `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_DECLINED` | Invite declined, to the proposer | `CHAT` | `dateId`, `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_CANCELLED` | Date cancelled, to the other user (reason in the text) | `DATE_DETAIL` | `dateId`, `matchId`, `conversationId` |

| `DATE_RATE_REQUEST` | Date marked completed (one day after it), to both users | `RATE_DATE` | `dateId`, `matchId` |
| `VERIFICATION_PASSED` / `VERIFICATION_REJECTED` | Face verification decided (automatic or by an admin) | `VERIFICATION` | `verificationId` |
| `ACCOUNT_WARNING` | An admin warned the user (warning text in `body`) | `WARNING` | `warningId` |
| `REPORT_REVIEWED` | A report the user filed was resolved (never reveals the outcome) | `NONE` | — |

| `ANNOUNCEMENT` | Admin broadcast | `NONE` | — |

request.description:
Super-admin only. Retrieves current admin-tunable settings for Python Face Verification Microservice (DF-03, D-194, D-205, D-209-211).

**Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/admin/settings/verification`

**Response attributes:**
- `mode` (string): Operating mode: `AI` (automated ONNX/YuNet/SFace verification), `HOLD` (auto-pass all), or `MANUAL` (route all to admin review).
- `matchPassThreshold` (number): Face match confidence threshold for auto-pass (default: 0.40).
- `matchReviewThreshold` (number): Lower bound threshold before outright reject (default: 0.25).
- `livenessThreshold` (number): MiniFASNet anti-spoofing liveness passing threshold (default: 0.70).
- `requireGesture` (boolean): Whether V-pose peace sign is required (default: true).
- `maxAttemptsPerDay` (integer): Maximum verification attempts per 24 hours (default: 5).
- `failsBeforeReview` (integer): Consecutive failures before routing to admin review queue (default: 3).
- `cooldownSeconds` (integer): Cooldown wait time in seconds between attempts (default: 60; 0 for none).
- `selfieRetentionDays` (integer): Days before verification selfie is auto-purged from storage (default: 30).
